requirements.requirement: Collect, organize and analyze NFL information with a complete requirements register.
requirements.evidence: Source-linked research workspaces and this canonical register exist; completeness is limited to verified sources.
requirements.next: Close data-rights and historical-feed gaps before claiming complete coverage.

requirements.requirement: Clean GitHub Pages dashboard with category subpages and readable tables.
requirements.evidence: Static pages, relative links, source column on every table row, responsive CSS and build checks.
requirements.next: Keep link/citation checks in CI.

requirements.requirement: Suggestions reviewed before implementation changes.
requirements.evidence: Dedicated suggestion board with recommended path, dependencies, trade-offs and optional browser-local review export.
requirements.next: Reviewer may approve/defer/reject; no selection silently deploys a strategy.

requirements.requirement: Clear questions, known information, missing answers and discovery actions.
requirements.evidence: Decision register separates known facts from unknowns and names the cheapest discovery action.
requirements.next: Answers requiring contracts, jurisdiction or budget remain open.

requirements.requirement: Originate independent NFL lines.
requirements.evidence: Existing research-desk contains exploratory community-data models; official-only validation inputs and licensed market history are not established.
requirements.next: Use the line-origination protocol only after official outcomes and permissioned prices pass gates.

requirements.requirement: Research useful signals for singles, parlays and player-prop combinations.
requirements.evidence: Testable hypotheses and validation design are documented; no strategy is approved.
requirements.next: Run pre-registered walk-forward tests on verified data.

requirements.requirement: Leaderboard competition with rewards for top strategies.
requirements.evidence: Gate-first ranking and reward rules are specified; eligible verified entries and reward funding are absent.
requirements.next: Withhold rewards until eligibility, legal review and funding are verified.

requirements.requirement: Every strategy passes validation gates.
requirements.evidence: Ten fail-closed gates cover provenance, timing, completeness, market rules, pre-registration, evaluation, dependence, personnel, shadow and rewards.
requirements.next: No live strategy has passed; synthetic unit tests are not performance evidence.

requirements.requirement: Determine correlation values.
requirements.evidence: No official-only matched leg-outcome sample is verified. Correlation cells remain blank.
requirements.next: Estimate pairwise and joint dependence from training games only; validate on held-out combinations.

requirements.requirement: Remove luck and reward selective skill.
requirements.evidence: Luck cannot be eliminated. Proper scores, game-cluster uncertainty, ablations, multiplicity control and prospective shadow records reduce false confidence.
requirements.next: Never label residual variance as pure luck or a hot streak as skill.

requirements.requirement: Track injuries and offensive/defensive starter replacements.
requirements.evidence: Official report snapshot and club depth evidence are separated; replacement assignment and workload remain blank without direct evidence.
requirements.next: Automate timestamped capture and flag stale/conflicting sources.

requirements.requirement: Identify 2nd/3rd/4th-string backup deficiencies.
requirements.evidence: Club depth lists can establish published order; deficiency requires role, participation and outcome evidence.
requirements.next: Do not infer a fixed points penalty from string rank alone.

requirements.requirement: Executive summary.
requirements.evidence: Summary states delivered work, blockers, recommended path and verification boundaries.
requirements.next: Update after material evidence changes.

requirements.requirement: No manual user input; autonomous completion.
requirements.evidence: Build, checks, capture workflow and publication are automated; contracts, budget and legal decisions cannot be invented.
requirements.next: Use conservative research-only defaults and leave unresolved decisions open.

requirements.requirement: Line-by-line official-source verification; blank unconfirmed values.
requirements.evidence: Canonical tables use official sources and blank unknowns. Independent audit flags community-data mislabeling in an existing workspace.
requirements.next: Treat digest integrity as separate from official factual verification.

requirements.requirement: Coordinate parallel sessions and avoid conflicts.
requirements.evidence: COORDINATION.md claims, append-only logs, fixed Arena branch and preserved concurrent workspaces.
requirements.next: Re-fetch before final merge; preserve other sessions' content.

requirements.requirement: PR, merge, Pages deployment and flagged-review page.
requirements.evidence: PR #23 merged as 9b4611a429ecf9640ea5373ec1780d9d3f0a6ab2; Pages validate/deploy run 43178027508 succeeded; live decision-lab page fetched.
requirements.next: Keep flagged items under review; hourly Pages refresh rebuilds and audits before publication.

requirements.requirement: Explain, for every official report row that cannot be joined to club depth evidence, why it is unjoined instead of guessing a replacement.
requirements.evidence: Availability analysis reports 254 report rows, 185 exact joins, 69 unmatched with a per-club reason and 117 published replacement leads.
requirements.next: Re-run the join once the Texans image chart and Packers number-prefixed chart are parsed.

requirements.requirement: Prove the injury report is structurally complete for every listed matchup before any availability signal is used.
requirements.evidence: 14 matchups x 2 clubs = 28 club sections, and 28 sections were captured (F4 check passes), including 4 explicit 'No Injuries Reported' sections.
requirements.next: Keep this check fail-closed when the report is recaptured.

requirements.requirement: Separate injury designation from confirmed non-participation and from confirmed backup usage.
requirements.evidence: Only 6 of 254 published rows carry a game designation at capture (5 Out, 1 Questionable). No active list or snap count is captured.
requirements.next: Add the official inactive list and snap counts; both change after the report.

requirements.requirement: Detect clubs where a ranked depth slot is itself depleted (multiple listed players on the report).
requirements.evidence: 147 published depth slots join to the report; 19 slots have 2+ listed players and 3 slots have 3+.
requirements.next: Rank slots by measured performance impact once snap data exists, not by count alone.

requirements.requirement: Verify the published values line by line against the live official source, and record unreachable sources as unverified rather than as passing.
requirements.evidence: Field-by-field comparison across 8 injury fields plus per-club depth tuple comparison; offline structural run passes, live run is executed in the publication workflow.
requirements.next: Attach the live verification artifact to each deployment.

requirements.requirement: Show, before implementation, the trade-off and dependency of every suggested change so a reviewer can choose a path.
requirements.evidence: Suggestions register with priority, effort, impact, dependency, trade-off, review state and exportable review file.
requirements.next: Record the reviewer's chosen path and date in COORDINATION.md.

requirements.requirement: Distinguish league-scheduled conditions (international game) and club turnover context from injuries before attributing performance change to backups.
requirements.evidence: The NFL scores page labels the Patriots at Lions Week 10 matchup as an International Game; no official turnover or roster-transaction feed is captured.
requirements.next: Capture official transaction and inactive reports so personnel change is measured, not assumed.

requirements.requirement: Keep every empirical betting number blank until a permissioned price and an official settlement source exist.
requirements.evidence: Line, probability, correlation and reward cells are published blank; 10 fail-closed gates reject rows without official provenance and settlement.
requirements.next: Revisit only when Q03 and Q04 are answered.

requirements.requirement: Show a reviewer the cost, benefit and blocking dependencies of each candidate path before any change is implemented.
requirements.evidence: Three candidate paths with prerequisites, cost, benefit, risk and a comparative table, plus a review-and-export workflow that cannot deploy anything.
requirements.next: Have a human record the chosen path and decision date in COORDINATION.md.

questions.question: Is this private research, public analytics, paid recommendations or wagering operations?
questions.known: The request is research/decision support and a public GitHub Pages site.
questions.missing: Jurisdiction, audience, monetization and whether stakes are handled.
questions.discovery: Default to analytics-only; obtain qualified legal review before any paid or wagering feature.

questions.question: Which spreads, totals, moneylines, team totals and player props are in scope?
questions.known: Singles, parlays and player-prop combinations are requested.
questions.missing: Exact market definitions, books, overtime/void/push rules and prop settlement.
questions.discovery: Create a market dictionary from permissioned book rules and official NFL scoring rules.

questions.question: Which provider permits historical and live odds retention, derived models and redistribution?
questions.known: NFL widgets display partner-supplied odds; no licensed archive is verified here.
questions.missing: Contract, API terms, latency, limits, prop coverage and retention rights.
questions.discovery: Request written vendor terms; compare coverage and cost without assuming access.

questions.question: What authoritative machine-readable source settles every target and market?
questions.known: NFL publishes scores, stats and season-specific rules.
questions.missing: Licensed export, correction policy and market-specific grading map.
questions.discovery: Map NFL game/player identifiers to book market IDs and test settlement on known cases.

questions.question: Can every feature be reconstructed as it was known before kickoff?
questions.known: Current injury pages and club depth charts are mutable.
questions.missing: Immutable snapshots, publication times, correction history and as-of joins.
questions.discovery: Capture raw-source hashes and timestamps on a schedule; never backfill from future pages.

questions.question: Which depth charts are official guidance, unofficial lists or confirmed lineups?
questions.known: Commanders/Giants publish club depth pages; Colts explicitly labels its Week 10 chart unofficial.
questions.missing: Confirmed starters, game-day actives and actual replacement participation.
questions.discovery: Store source authority separately; join inactive lists and participation only when verified.

questions.question: How much does a specific replacement change expected performance?
questions.known: Depth order alone does not measure quality or workload.
questions.missing: Role-specific snaps, opponent-adjusted outcomes and enough replacement cases.
questions.discovery: Estimate effects from verified historical participation with uncertainty; abstain when sparse.

questions.question: How should Questionable, Doubtful, Out and blank status be encoded?
questions.known: NFL policy defines the labels; blank game status is not a probability.
questions.missing: Empirical availability calibration by status, timing and team.
questions.discovery: Keep categorical labels; estimate probabilities only from point-in-time training data.

questions.question: What happens when NFL.com, a club chart and a news article disagree?
questions.known: Week 10 sources show status/depth lags and missing players.
questions.missing: A reconciled, timestamped authority policy.
questions.discovery: Preserve both observations, flag the conflict and suppress affected model inputs.

questions.question: What model family and uncertainty method produce the independent number?
questions.known: A transparent baseline plus opponent/context adjustments is testable; no family is validated.
questions.missing: Verified training sample, feature definitions, calibration and holdout results.
questions.discovery: Pre-register a simple baseline first; expand only if held-out skill improves.

questions.question: Which leg pairs are dependent and how stable is the dependence?
questions.known: Same-game outcomes can share game script; no verified correlation value is available.
questions.missing: Matched binary leg outcomes, joint events, sample counts and conditional groups.
questions.discovery: Estimate phi/Pearson association and direct joint probability on training games; bootstrap by game.

questions.question: Can joint probability and payout be verified without an independence shortcut?
questions.known: Multiplying marginal probabilities is invalid when legs are dependent.
questions.missing: Book combo price, void rules, joint settlement and held-out joint calibration.
questions.discovery: Price from validated joint outcomes; compare with independence baseline and reject sparse pairs.

questions.question: Are prop lines, participation and settlement available at the decision timestamp?
questions.known: NFL tracking glossary defines useful metrics but is not a prop feed.
questions.missing: Historical prop quotes, player IDs, minutes/snaps, void rules and book coverage.
questions.discovery: Secure permissioned prop history and official participation labels before modeling.

questions.question: What minimum evidence is required before a strategy is eligible?
questions.known: Thresholds must be declared before viewing results; this site proposes conservative design defaults.
questions.missing: Owner-approved sample, risk, calibration and shadow policy.
questions.discovery: Use the published proposed gates as research defaults; do not claim they are league rules.

questions.question: How many strategies and feature variants were tried?
questions.known: Leaderboard selection inflates apparent performance.
questions.missing: Complete trial registry including failed and abandoned variants.
questions.discovery: Hash pre-registrations and apply family-wise multiplicity control before ranking.

questions.question: Can luck be removed from the evaluation?
questions.known: No. Randomness remains; uncertainty can be quantified and false confidence reduced.
questions.answer: Luck cannot be eliminated; require out-of-sample, uncertainty-aware evidence.
questions.missing: Prospective verified forecast record and stable benchmark improvement.
questions.discovery: Use proper scores, game-cluster intervals, ablations and shadow follow-up.

questions.question: What score determines the winner?
questions.known: Raw win rate and short-run ROI are inadequate.
questions.missing: Approved scoring rule, benchmark, stake policy and minimum activity.
questions.discovery: Propose benchmark-relative Brier skill with uncertainty and gate eligibility; keep divisions separate.

questions.question: Who funds rewards and what legal rules apply?
questions.known: No reward pool, payment system or legal approval is verified.
questions.missing: Budget, eligibility, tax/legal review and dispute process.
questions.discovery: Publish recognition-only leaderboard until funding and compliance are confirmed.

questions.question: Can ingestion run without manual entry and survive source changes?
questions.known: GitHub Actions can schedule captures and build static pages; Pages has no backend database.
questions.missing: Durable history storage, alerting, rights and source SLA.
questions.discovery: Use scheduled official captures with hashes; add durable storage only after retention review.

questions.question: Are nflverse release assets official NFL data?
questions.known: They are community-maintained GitHub releases; a digest proves byte integrity, not NFL authorship.
questions.answer: No official NFL authority is established for those assets in this review.
questions.missing: NFL endorsement/license or row-level official confirmation.
questions.discovery: Label community outputs exploratory/unverified and exclude them from official-only gates.

questions.question: How are suggestions approved without accidental deployment?
questions.known: The suggestion board can record optional browser-local choices and export JSON.
questions.missing: Server-side identity, durable approvals and change-control integration.
questions.discovery: Treat exports as review artifacts; require a separate tracked change before implementation.

questions.question: Will accounts, payments or sensitive betting activity be collected?
questions.known: This site is static and collects no account or wagering data.
questions.missing: Future product scope and privacy/legal requirements.
questions.discovery: Keep data minimization; threat-model any future backend before adding it.

questions.question: Should the Texans image-based depth chart be manually transcribed, or is there an official text/XML endpoint?
questions.known: The club page is headed 'Unofficial Depth Chart' and publishes the chart as an image; no table is present.
questions.missing: Whether the club or the league exposes a structured depth feed, and who is authorized to transcribe an image into data.
questions.discovery: Ask the club/league for a structured feed; until then leave the 13 Texans rows unmatched rather than transcribing by eye.

questions.question: Should jersey-number prefixes be stripped before name matching on club depth pages?
questions.known: The Packers chart places jersey numbers before names (for example '9 Christian Watson') and repeats a player across slots (Kitan Oladapo at both safeties). The live check fetched the page but extracted 0 rows, so the parser — not the published data — is the blocker.
questions.missing: A documented, reversible rule plus a stored original string for audit.
questions.discovery: Add number-stripping with the raw published string preserved, and unit-test both forms.

questions.question: What is the minimum evidence that a backup, rather than the listed starter, actually took the snaps?
questions.known: No active list, snap count share or participation report is captured. A published rank is not proof of usage.
questions.missing: Official inactive lists, snap counts and any club statement of role change.
questions.discovery: Capture official inactive lists pre-kickoff and snap counts post-game into an immutable per-game record.

questions.question: How should the International Game designation be modelled in team-strength and availability models?
questions.known: The NFL scores page labels Patriots at Lions (Week 10, 2026) as an International Game and lists this week at 14 matchups.
questions.missing: Any evidence of a measurable travel/venue effect on personnel usage or performance.
questions.discovery: Model it as an explicit covariate and test whether it adds skill; do not add a fixed penalty without evidence.

questions.question: Which target defines 'the best path' when no price data exists: forecast skill against a baseline, or agreement with the market?
questions.known: No permissioned price history exists, so market-relative skill cannot currently be computed.
questions.missing: An agreed primary metric and a fallback that is not a proxy for profitability.
questions.discovery: Pre-register a proper-score primary metric against a frozen baseline (Brier/log loss with game-cluster intervals) and treat market comparison as a later gate.

questions.question: Which official event should invalidate a captured depth chart: a trade, a signing, an injury designation or the inactive list?
questions.known: The Colts' own Week 10 release documents two starting-receiver trades and a practice-squad signing in the same article as the depth chart.
questions.missing: An event feed with timestamps and a rule for which events force a re-capture before a decision is made.
questions.discovery: Subscribe to official transaction and inactive sources; version each depth capture against the last roster event and re-verify on change.

questions.question: When the live official page has moved on to a later week, is a row difference drift, staleness or an extraction error?
questions.known: A live run compared a Week 10 capture against a page that had advanced, producing 41 apparent row differences that the data does not actually explain.
questions.missing: An agreed definition of each category and a rule for when a capture must be re-versioned instead of compared.
questions.discovery: Classify every difference as capture-time, source-time or extraction-time; only extraction errors fail a gate, and all three are published.

suggestions.title: Adopt an official-only evidence contract
suggestions.detail: Separate source authority, byte integrity and model validation. Community data may be exploratory only; canonical decision values require official confirmation.
suggestions.tradeoff: Some existing exploratory numbers become non-decision evidence.
suggestions.success_metric: Accepts the contract in a recorded decision and shows it on the site's decision page.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Every decision row carries an official source or is blank and flagged.

suggestions.title: Secure permissioned odds and prop history
suggestions.detail: Obtain written terms for historical/live prices, limits, timestamps, props, retention and derived data.
suggestions.tradeoff: Cost and vendor selection remain unresolved; do not scrape around rights.
suggestions.success_metric: Names the provider and the permitted uses in a recorded decision.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: A signed agreement exists and a timestamped price can be stored.

suggestions.title: Build immutable official availability snapshots
suggestions.detail: Scheduled capture of NFL injury reports, club depth pages and inactive evidence with raw hashes, timestamps and conflict flags.
suggestions.tradeoff: Public pages can change or block automation; durable storage needs review.
suggestions.success_metric: Approves daily capture with retained hashes.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: At least one capture per day per source, never silently overwritten.

suggestions.title: Start with a singles-only shadow baseline
suggestions.impact: Creates a clean benchmark before complexity
suggestions.detail: Pre-register a simple team-strength model, freeze versions and record forecasts before kickoff.
suggestions.tradeoff: No immediate betting recommendations or rewards.
suggestions.success_metric: Approves a singles-only prospective trial.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: A frozen pre-registration plus a complete prospective ledger.

suggestions.title: Add injury/depth ablations, not fixed penalties
suggestions.impact: Tests whether personnel information adds skill
suggestions.detail: Compare identical models with and without verified availability features using chronological holdouts.
suggestions.tradeoff: Sparse replacement cases may force abstention.
suggestions.success_metric: Approves the ablation study design.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: An ablation delta is reported with a cluster lower bound.

suggestions.title: Delay parlays until joint outcomes validate
suggestions.detail: Require matched leg outcomes, direct joint calibration, game-cluster uncertainty and book payout rules.
suggestions.tradeoff: Slower expansion into requested combo markets.
suggestions.success_metric: Keeps combos blocked until joint evidence exists.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Zero combo rows without a joint probability and settlement rule.

suggestions.title: Use proper-score leaderboard divisions
suggestions.detail: Separate singles, game parlays, same-game parlays and prop combos; rank eligible strategies by benchmark-relative skill with uncertainty.
suggestions.tradeoff: Requires minimum sample and complete trial registry.
suggestions.success_metric: Approves proper-score ranking by division.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: No entry ranked without an interval and a trial count.

suggestions.title: Keep rewards recognition-only until approved
suggestions.detail: No money, credits or stake handling until budget, jurisdiction and legal review are verified.
suggestions.tradeoff: No monetary competition at launch.
suggestions.success_metric: Records the recognition-only policy.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: No live page promises a prize or accepts stakes.

suggestions.title: Publish a conflict-aware review queue
suggestions.detail: Flag source lags, authority gaps, missing ranks and unsupported claims with official links and discovery actions.
suggestions.tradeoff: Flags do not block publication but block affected decisions.
suggestions.success_metric: Approves the review queue with sources.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Every flag has a source link, an action and a severity.

suggestions.title: Automate build, citation and link gates
suggestions.detail: Fail CI on missing row sources, broken local links, duplicate IDs, conflict markers or unsupported verified badges.
suggestions.tradeoff: External content still needs scheduled re-verification.
suggestions.success_metric: Approves the automated gates.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Every deployment runs the citation and link checks and fails closed.

suggestions.title: Add durable snapshot storage and alerts
suggestions.detail: Store immutable captures outside the static site, monitor freshness and alert on source/schema changes.
suggestions.tradeoff: Hosting, retention and access controls need a decision.
suggestions.success_metric: Approves storage scope and cost.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: A verified change event triggers a timestamped notification.

suggestions.title: Expand to player-prop combinations last
suggestions.impact: Addresses the hardest requested market safely
suggestions.detail: Require verified participation, prop settlement, joint dependence and held-out calibration before any combo signal.
suggestions.tradeoff: Highest data and overfit burden; no launch date is promised.
suggestions.success_metric: Defers props until singles and combos are validated.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: No prop row is published without permissioned prop and settlement data.

suggestions.title: Adopt an official-only evidence contract
suggestions.detail: Separate three different claims: source authority (who published it), capture integrity (did the bytes change) and model validity (does it forecast). Only official NFL/club pages may support a decision value; community data stays exploratory.
suggestions.tradeoff: Some existing exploratory numbers stop counting as decision evidence.
suggestions.success_metric: 100% of decision rows carry an official HTTPS source or are blank and listed on the flagged page.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Every downstream decision inherits an unverifiable foundation.

suggestions.title: Secure permissioned odds and prop history
suggestions.recommendation: Start only if product scope is legal
suggestions.detail: Any line origination or leaderboard needs a timestamped price series with documented redistribution rights. Without it, skill can only be measured against a baseline, not against the market.
suggestions.tradeoff: Cost and legal review; may not be obtainable at all.
suggestions.success_metric: A signed data agreement plus a stored, timestamped price per market and event.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Line origination, correlations and the leaderboard stay structurally blocked.

suggestions.title: Automate immutable multi-day availability snapshots
suggestions.impact: Turns a single snapshot into a time series
suggestions.detail: Capture the official report and club depth pages at least daily with retained hashes, so practice designations can be replayed as they were known. Today the site holds one capture, which cannot support backtesting.
suggestions.tradeoff: Storage and rate-limit care; stale pages must be versioned, not overwritten.
suggestions.success_metric: At least one capture per day per source with a retained hash and no silent overwrite.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: No historical availability study is possible next week either.

suggestions.title: Fix the two depth-parsing failures before widening coverage
suggestions.detail: The Texans publish depth as an image and the Packers prepend jersey numbers. Number stripping plus storing the raw string recovers the Packers rows; the Texans image needs an authorized structured source, not transcription by eye.
suggestions.tradeoff: Image transcription is manual and non-authoritative if done carelessly.
suggestions.success_metric: Unmatched rows fall from 69 to at most 40 with every remaining row explained per club.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Availability signals silently under-represent two clubs.

suggestions.title: Capture official inactive lists and snap counts
suggestions.recommendation: Approve; it is the missing link
suggestions.detail: Only 6 of 254 report rows carry a game designation, and no active list or snap share is captured. Without them a backup's replacement of a starter cannot be confirmed, only suspected.
suggestions.tradeoff: Most data arrives after kickoff, so pre-game decisions cannot use it.
suggestions.success_metric: Every played game has an inactive list and snap shares stored per player.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Replacement-deficiency strategies remain untestable.

suggestions.title: Start with a singles-only shadow baseline
suggestions.impact: Creates the first honest skill measurement
suggestions.detail: Pre-register one simple opponent/context baseline, log forecasts prospectively before kickoff, and score with proper scores and game-cluster intervals. No stake, no payout, no posting a leaderboard position yet.
suggestions.tradeoff: Slow: needs 128+ shadow games before any eligibility claim.
suggestions.success_metric: A frozen pre-registration plus a complete prospective ledger with zero post-hoc edits.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Every later strategy inherits an unmeasured baseline.

suggestions.title: Model depth slots as groups, not a single starter
suggestions.detail: 149 club/unit/position slots list more than one rank-1 player (three receivers at rank 1, three inside linebackers at rank 1). Treating column 1 as 'the starter' would fabricate a starter the club never named.
suggestions.tradeoff: Slightly more complex joins and displays.
suggestions.success_metric: No page states that a named player is the confirmed starter without an explicit club statement.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Personnel signals are wrong for many of the highest-volume positions.

suggestions.title: Add injury and personnel ablations instead of fixed penalties
suggestions.detail: Instead of subtracting a fixed number of points for a missing starter, test the same model with and without the personnel features and report the difference with uncertainty.
suggestions.tradeoff: Requires enough games to detect a small effect; may find no effect.
suggestions.success_metric: A reported ablation delta with a cluster lower bound, positive or negative.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Personnel factors remain an untested belief.

suggestions.title: Keep parlays and prop combos behind a joint-evidence gate
suggestions.detail: Multiplying marginal probabilities is invalid under dependence. A combo may only be ranked when a directly validated joint probability and the operator's void/push rules are both available.
suggestions.tradeoff: Some attractive-looking combos are simply not rankable.
suggestions.success_metric: Zero combo rows without a joint probability and a settlement rule.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: A dependent parlay can look profitable while losing on structure.

suggestions.title: Rank with proper scores and uncertainty, not win rate
suggestions.impact: Makes the leaderboard resistant to luck
suggestions.detail: Rank by benchmark-relative Brier skill with a game-cluster lower bound and a multiplicity adjustment for the number of trials. Raw win rate and short-run ROI cannot distinguish skill from variance.
suggestions.tradeoff: Fewer entries qualify at first; a leaderboard may look empty.
suggestions.success_metric: No entry is ranked without an interval and a trial count.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: The first hot streak becomes the apparent winner.

suggestions.title: Keep rewards recognition-only until funded and reviewed
suggestions.impact: Avoids an unfunded or unlawful prize promise
suggestions.detail: No reward funding, tax treatment or jurisdiction analysis exists. Publish the leaderboard as recognition only; any prize requires legal and financial approval first.
suggestions.tradeoff: Less motivating than a prize.
suggestions.success_metric: No live page promises a prize or accepts stakes.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: An implied prize could create legal exposure.

suggestions.title: Publish a conflict-aware review queue with sources
suggestions.impact: Makes disagreement visible instead of hidden
suggestions.detail: Every irregularity, unreachable source and unverified cell is published with its source link and an action, and none of them silently blocks publication.
suggestions.tradeoff: A visibly imperfect site.
suggestions.success_metric: Every flag has a source link, an action and a severity.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Irregularities are discovered by the user, in production.

suggestions.title: Automate verification in CI, including a live re-fetch
suggestions.impact: Detects source drift without manual work
suggestions.detail: Run the offline structural checks on every pull request and the live field-by-field re-fetch on a schedule and before deployment, publishing the result as an artifact and a page.
suggestions.tradeoff: Live checks can fail for transient network reasons; they must report unreachable, not failed-match.
suggestions.success_metric: Every deployment carries a verification artifact with per-family status.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: The published snapshot silently drifts from the official source.

suggestions.title: Add durable storage and change alerts
suggestions.impact: Enables alerting instead of manual checks
suggestions.detail: Static hosting has no database. Durable storage plus a scheduled job is required before an alert on an injury or depth change can be sent.
suggestions.tradeoff: Adds infrastructure and cost beyond GitHub Pages.
suggestions.success_metric: A verified change event triggers a timestamped notification.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: The site stays a snapshot rather than a monitor.

suggestions.title: Treat roster turnover as a first-class data event
suggestions.impact: Keeps depth evidence from going stale
suggestions.detail: The Colts' Week 10 release documents two starting-receiver trades in the same article as its depth chart. Depth, availability and lineup evidence must be versioned against the last official roster event, not trusted as durable.
suggestions.tradeoff: More frequent re-capture and reconciliation work.
suggestions.success_metric: Every depth capture records the roster event that most recently preceded it.
suggestions.risk_if_delayed: Signals reference players who are no longer on the roster.

strategies.name: Opponent-adjusted team strength
strategies.hypothesis: Rolling offense/defense efficiency with opponent and context adjustments improves spread/total forecasts versus a simple baseline.
strategies.inputs: Official game outcomes, possessions/context, as-of features and permissioned prices.
strategies.test: Walk-forward by game; compare Brier/log loss and calibration against frozen baseline and market.
strategies.risk: Schedule strength, garbage time and small samples.

strategies.name: Quarterback availability shock
strategies.hypothesis: Confirmed QB absence/replacement changes team scoring enough to create incremental forecast value.
strategies.inputs: Timestamped injury/inactive evidence, confirmed replacement, historical participation and prices.
strategies.test: Ablate availability feature; cluster uncertainty by game; require held-out improvement.
strategies.risk: Status is not playing probability; replacement quality varies.

strategies.name: Offensive-line replacement stress
strategies.hypothesis: Multiple verified OL replacements degrade protection/run efficiency beyond what the market prices.
strategies.inputs: Position-specific depth, actives, snaps, pressure/sack outcomes and market prices.
strategies.test: Role-weighted exposure model versus unweighted injury count; chronological holdout.
strategies.risk: String rank alone is not a deficiency estimate.

strategies.name: Secondary replacement exposure
strategies.hypothesis: Verified defensive-back replacements affect passing efficiency and scoring conditional on coverage role.
strategies.inputs: Depth/actives, participation, opponent-adjusted passing outcomes and prices.
strategies.test: Compare defense-exposure feature ablation with game-cluster intervals.
strategies.risk: Rotation and scheme confounding; sparse cases.

strategies.name: Pace and possession efficiency
strategies.hypothesis: Neutral pace and points-per-possession improve total forecasts over raw points per game.
strategies.inputs: Official play/context data or licensed verified equivalents; prices and settlement.
strategies.test: Pre-registered total model; held-out calibration and market comparison.
strategies.risk: Pace and efficiency can be endogenous to score script.

strategies.name: Cross-game parlay value
strategies.hypothesis: Only combinations with verified joint pricing and demonstrated dependence treatment may have value.
strategies.inputs: Timestamped combo prices, leg outcomes, void/push rules and joint sample.
strategies.test: Direct joint probability versus independence baseline; held-out joint Brier score.
strategies.risk: Cross-game independence is an assumption, not a verified fact.

strategies.name: Same-game script combination
strategies.hypothesis: Game-script-linked legs require conditional joint modeling rather than multiplying marginals.
strategies.inputs: Matched same-game leg outcomes, combo payout rules and prices.
strategies.test: Estimate dependence on training games; validate joint calibration and payout EV out of sample.
strategies.risk: Strong dependence, sparse combos and book margin.

strategies.name: Receiver opportunity prop
strategies.hypothesis: Verified target-share/air-yard changes under personnel shifts may improve reception/yardage forecasts.
strategies.inputs: NGS definitions, licensed tracking/participation, prop quotes and settlement.
strategies.test: Player-grouped chronological validation; compare with book-implied probability.
strategies.risk: Role changes, coverage and void rules.

strategies.name: Rushing workload prop combo
strategies.hypothesis: Confirmed replacement workload and game script may jointly affect rushing attempts/yards.
strategies.inputs: Depth/actives, snap counts, rush outcomes, prop lines and joint settlement.
strategies.test: Joint outcome model with game-cluster bootstrap and independence comparison.

strategies.name: Injury-news timing reaction
strategies.hypothesis: Forecasts updated only after verified status changes may beat stale baselines if execution is feasible.
strategies.inputs: Immutable report timestamps, quote timestamps, latency/limits and settlement.
strategies.test: Event-time study with no future information; execution-cost stress test.
strategies.risk: Market may react first; stale or revised reports cause leakage.

gates.name: Official provenance
gates.rule: Every decision input has an official source URL, retrieval time, raw hash and field-level confirmation; community data is excluded from official-only claims.
gates.fail: Missing authority, hash mismatch or inferred value.

gates.name: As-of integrity
gates.rule: Feature availability and quote timestamps precede forecast time; forecast precedes kickoff; training games end before holdout games.
gates.fail: Future information, overlapping game clusters or retrospective edits.

gates.name: Completeness
gates.rule: Required fields, identifiers, coverage and duplicate checks pass; unknown cells remain blank and flagged.
gates.fail: Silent imputation, duplicate events or missing settlement.

gates.name: Market executability
gates.rule: Permissioned timestamped price, limits/latency, vig, push/void and settlement rules are documented.
gates.fail: No actionable price or unverifiable grading.

gates.name: Pre-registration
gates.rule: Model version, feature set, thresholds, benchmark and complete trial family are hashed before evaluation.
gates.fail: Post-hoc rule changes or hidden failed trials.

gates.name: Out-of-sample skill
gates.rule: Walk-forward proper-score improvement over a frozen baseline survives game-cluster uncertainty and multiplicity adjustment.
gates.fail: Uncertainty includes no improvement, or evidence disappears in untouched holdout.

gates.name: Dependence / combos
gates.rule: Matched joint outcomes validate direct joint probability and dependence against an independence baseline.
gates.fail: Sparse pairs, marginal-only pricing or test-set correlation fitting.

gates.name: Personnel robustness
gates.rule: Availability features use dated official/club evidence with authority labels; conflicts or stale sources trigger abstention.
gates.fail: Depth rank inferred from injury listing or fixed unsupported penalty.

gates.name: Prospective shadow
gates.rule: Frozen forecasts are logged before outcomes and monitored for drift, calibration and freshness.
gates.fail: No independent prospective record or changed rules after seeing results.

gates.name: Reward eligibility
gates.rule: Only strategies passing G01-G09 enter a division leaderboard; rewards require approved funding and legal policy.
gates.fail: Raw win-rate ranking, lucky streak reward or unresolved dispute.

flags.title: NFL authority is unverified for GitHub-hosted data
flags.finding: Repository code describes nflverse GitHub release assets as official NFL data. The local manifest checks GitHub-published SHA-256 digests, which confirms byte integrity only; this review did not find NFL authorship or authorization evidence. This is not a finding that the data are inaccurate.
flags.action: Treat these outputs as authority-unverified and exploratory; exclude them from official-only gates/rewards unless NFL provenance and data-use permission are independently confirmed.

flags.title: No verified historical odds/prop archive
flags.finding: NFL Support confirms partner-supplied widgets, not a licensed historical feed or settlement archive.
flags.action: Obtain permissioned market history before CLV, ROI or parlay EV claims.

flags.title: Depth charts are not confirmed participation
flags.finding: Club charts can be unofficial or lag injury reports; Colts explicitly labels its Week 10 chart unofficial.
flags.action: Keep authority, rank, active status and workload separate; blank missing fields.

flags.title: Injury source lags and conflicts
flags.finding: NFL.com report/article and club depth pages can disagree on availability or listed players.
flags.action: Preserve both timestamps and flag conflicts; suppress affected signals.

flags.title: No empirical correlation or validated strategy
flags.finding: Canonical official-only matched leg outcomes and prospective records are absent; correlation and performance cells are blank.
flags.action: Run the documented protocol only after data gates pass.

flags.title: Luck cannot be eliminated
flags.finding: Residual variance contains chance, opponent effects and model error; it is not a pure luck estimate.
flags.action: Use uncertainty, ablations, multiplicity control and shadow validation; avoid certainty claims.

flags.title: Rewards lack funding and legal approval
flags.finding: No reward pool, jurisdiction analysis or payment compliance is verified.
flags.action: Recognition-only until approved; no stake handling.

flags.title: Static hosting has no durable backend
flags.finding: GitHub Pages serves static files; scheduled Actions are not a guaranteed real-time database or alerting service.
flags.action: Use immutable captures and add durable storage/alerting after retention review.

flags.title: Current report is not a historical archive
flags.finding: The Week 10 injury page changes and does not provide point-in-time reconstruction by itself.
flags.action: Store retrieval time and raw hash for every capture; never backfill from a later page.

flags.title: Review choices are browser-local
flags.finding: Suggestion selections/export do not create server-side approval or deploy changes.
flags.action: Use exported JSON as a review artifact and require a tracked implementation change.

flags.title: Parallel-session overlap and coordination noise
flags.finding: Multiple sessions began from the same empty baseline and produced overlapping dashboards; append-only logs preserve the history.
flags.action: Keep canonical decision tables here and preserve other workspaces as linked research archives.

flags.title: Official source links are not reuse permission
flags.finding: Public NFL/club pages establish facts for review but do not by themselves grant redistribution, API or commercial rights.
flags.action: Confirm terms before bulk republication or commercial automation.

flags.title: Depth cells with two players were joined into one name
flags.finding: The depth capturer concatenated the text of each published table cell. Some club pages publish two players in one cell (for example Steelers TE1 'Pat Freiermuth' and 'Darnell Washington'; Seahawks WR1 'Cooper Kupp' and 'Rashid Shaheed'). Published rows therefore contained non-existent players such as 'Pat Freiermuth Darnell Washington'. 22 captured rows are affected.
flags.action: The parser now emits one row per published anchor. Already-captured rows are kept exactly as published and flagged as unverified on the Verification log; they are not split, because splitting on whitespace cannot tell a second player from a suffix or an initial. A fresh capture clears them.

flags.title: Self-declared unofficial depth charts were labelled plain official charts
flags.finding: The Patriots depth page states its 2026 chart 'is unofficial and is published by the writers of Patriots.com'. Its 62 captured rows carried the same plain 'club depth chart' authority label as charts with no such caveat. The Colts rows were already labelled UNOFFICIAL, so the label existed but was not applied consistently.
flags.action: The capturer now reads the page's own wording and labels such charts UNOFFICIAL, storing the page's sentence as an authority caveat. Already-captured rows keep their recorded label until a fresh capture.

flags.title: Texans depth chart is an image, so 13 report rows cannot be joined
flags.finding: The Houston Texans publish their depth page as a rendered image headed 'Unofficial Depth Chart', with no player/rank table in the HTML. The live automated check therefore cannot read it, and the current capture holds no parsed Texans depth rows, so the club's report rows cannot be joined.
flags.action: Keep those rows unmatched and visibly flagged. Request a structured feed; add image transcription only with an authorized, auditable process.

flags.title: Packers depth page is published in a layout the parser does not read
flags.finding: The live re-check fetched https://www.packers.com/team/depth-chart successfully but extracted 0 depth rows, and the current capture holds no parsed Packers rows for 17 report players (for example '9 Christian Watson' with jersey numbers inside the cell, plus duplicated players across two slots such as Kitan Oladapo at both safety positions). The parser gap, not the existence of the data, is what leaves the club unjoined.
flags.action: Fix the parser for this layout, store the raw published string alongside the parsed name, and re-run the join; do not transcribe by eye.

flags.title: Published depth rank is ambiguous across 149 slots
flags.finding: 149 club/unit/position slots list more than one rank-1 player (for example three wide receivers all at rank 1, and three inside linebackers all at rank 1). 'Rank 1' therefore means 'first column', not 'the single starter'.
flags.action: Model depth slots as groups, never as a single starter pointer, and store the published column with the raw row.

flags.title: Injury designation is sparse at capture, so absence cannot be inferred
flags.finding: Only 6 of 254 published rows carry a game designation (5 Out, 1 Questionable). The NFL policy says a player certain to play is not listed in the game status report, so a blank designation is not evidence of health.
flags.action: Never encode a blank designation as 'active'. Require the inactive list before any availability claim.

flags.title: Availability analysis is a snapshot, not a point-in-time archive
flags.finding: The captured report is a single moment in Week 10. Practice designations change daily and the page is not a historical archive; a single capture cannot support backtesting.
flags.action: Schedule at least daily captures with retained hashes before any historical study; label the current analysis as a snapshot.

flags.title: Position-family mapping is an editorial choice
flags.finding: The availability join maps published position labels to families (for example RUSH, SAM, WILL and MIKE to LB/DL). 'RUSH' is currently unmapped and is reported rather than forced into a family.
flags.action: Keep the mapping explicit and versioned; treat any unmapped label as a visible gap, not a default.

flags.title: Colts publish depth two ways, and name formats differ from the NFL report
flags.finding: The Colts publish a tabular chart at /team/depth-chart and an unofficial list in a news article. The live check initially compared the article rows against the page URL and reported 50 false mismatches; the verifier now dispatches the correct parser per source. Separately, the article writes 'AJ Haulcy' where the NFL report writes 'A.J. Haulcy', and the Chiefs write 'Chig Okonkwo' where the report writes 'Chigoziem Okonkwo' — real name-format differences that break exact joins.
flags.action: Use one documented normalization step that keeps both raw strings, unit-tested, and never fuzzy-match across clubs.

flags.title: Roster turnover invalidates depth evidence the moment it is published
flags.finding: The same Colts release that publishes the Week 10 depth chart states the club traded two starting wide receivers (Keenan Allen to the 49ers, Josh Downs to the Chiefs) and signed a receiver from the practice squad. A captured depth page is therefore stale relative to roster moves and cannot be assumed current.
flags.action: Capture the official transaction/inactive trail with timestamps and version depth evidence per roster event; never treat a depth snapshot as durable.

flags.title: A verification tool reported false drift in production
flags.finding: The first live run of the automated integrity check compared Colts depth rows parsed from a news article against the club's tabular page, reporting 50 mismatches that were an artefact of the check, not of the data. The run also showed 41 report rows on the live page versus 254 in the capture, because the live NFL report had moved on to the next week.
flags.action: The verifier now dispatches a parser per source and a test pins that dispatch. Timeline differences are separated from extraction errors and published as their own category rather than as data drift.

flags.title: GitHub Pages is published by two mechanisms that can race
flags.finding: The repository deploys with actions/deploy-pages, but the Pages site is also configured with build_type 'legacy' (source: main branch, path /). Two publishers compete: a failed legacy pages-build-deployment run was observed while the Actions deployment succeeded. The API returned HTTP 403 for the attempt to switch build_type to 'workflow' from an automated token, so this cannot be changed from CI.
flags.action: Repository owner: Settings -> Pages -> Build and deployment -> Source: 'GitHub Actions'. Until then, treat a single failed pages-build-deployment run as superseded when the 'Validate and deploy GitHub Pages' run is green, and check the live URL for the expected page.

paths.name: Foundation first (recommended)
paths.summary: Fix provenance, parsing and verification; publish the review queue; keep every empirical number blank.
paths.prerequisites: Official-source contract, automated snapshots, corrected depth parsing.
paths.cost: Low to medium engineering; no data purchase.
paths.benefit: Every later number is auditable and the site can be trusted as a decision aid.
paths.recommended_for: The current state: verified facts, no price data.

paths.name: Gated research expansion
paths.summary: Add singles shadow trials, ablations and proper-score ranking once price and availability evidence exist.
paths.prerequisites: Path A complete, plus permissioned prices and inactive/snap data.
paths.cost: Medium to high; data agreement and sustained capture.
paths.benefit: The first honest skill measurement and the only route to a defensible leaderboard.
paths.risk: Months of evidence before any claim; may find no exploitable skill.
paths.recommended_for: After Path A and after Q03/Q04 are answered.

paths.name: Market-facing product
paths.summary: Publish originated lines, combos and prizes to an audience.
paths.prerequisites: Path B, legal review, funded rewards, redistribution rights for every data source.
paths.risk: Regulatory exposure, unfunded prize liability, reputational risk from weak evidence.
paths.recommended_for: Not now. Blocking answers Q01, Q03, Q18 are unanswered.
